note: The change-request mix for Phase 0. docs/lora-operator-guide.md §7 names this as a HUMAN judgment call — 'whether the generated change requests are realistic ... the mix should look like what a real user asks, not what was easy to generate'. So it is an editable, reviewable list, not a heuristic buried in code. Edit this file, re-run `pnpm lora:dataset`, and the mix changes. Each recipe declares the node roles it needs; the generator fills those slots ONLY from real nodes in that repo's scan, so a request can never name something that does not exist (a request that hallucinates teaches the model to hallucinate). `weight` biases how often a family is drawn when a repo can satisfy many recipes. `why` is the reason the family is in the mix at all — delete a recipe whose reason you disagree with.

families.cache: Read-path caching. The single most common architecture ask in the wild, and the one buildLocalArchProposal already special-cases — so the tuned model must be at least as good as the keyless fallback.
families.split: Decomposition. 'This thing does too much.' Exercises addCards anchored to an existing service plus edges back to it.
families.events: Asynchronous decoupling. The only family that exercises the `topic` card kind and the queue_publish/queue_consume edge inference.
families.edge: Ingress concerns — gateways, rate limits, auth in front of public traffic. Exercises an added service that fronts an existing one.
families.storage: Datastore topology: own database, read replica, audit log. Exercises the datastore card kind and db_read/db_write inference.
families.retire: Removal. The ONLY family that exercises removeCardIds. Rare in real chat but structurally distinct, so the model must not learn that the field is always empty.
families.observability: Cross-cutting sinks — metrics, tracing, audit. Realistic, and produces fan-in edges rather than the usual fan-out.

recipes.text: Add a read cache in front of {0.label} (`{0.id}`) so repeated lookups stop hitting it every time. Where would it sit?
recipes.why: The canonical ask. One new datastore card anchored to a real service, one edge.

recipes.text: {0.label} (`{0.id}`) reads from {1.label} (`{1.id}`) on every request. Put a cache between them.
recipes.why: Two real endpoints, a new node in the middle — the model must anchor to one and edge to both.

recipes.text: {0.label} (`{0.id}`) has grown too big. Split the read side out into its own service and show me the result.
recipes.why: Decomposition anchored on a real service; tests that new ids are prop:-prefixed rather than reusing the parent's.

recipes.text: {0.label} (`{0.id}`) and {1.label} (`{1.id}`) both duplicate the same logic. Pull it out into a shared service they both call.
recipes.why: Two real anchors, fan-in from both — a shape the single-anchor recipes never produce.

recipes.text: Put an event stream between {0.label} (`{0.id}`) and {1.label} (`{1.id}`) instead of the direct call, so a slow consumer can't stall the producer.
recipes.why: The `topic` card kind plus publish/consume edges — the only path that exercises queue edge inference.

recipes.text: {0.label} (`{0.id}`) can lose writes if it crashes mid-request. Add a durable outbox so events survive a restart.
recipes.why: Durability language rather than 'queue' language; keeps the model from keying on one keyword.

recipes.text: Give {0.label} (`{0.id}`) a work queue in front of it so bursts get absorbed instead of dropped.
recipes.why: A topic anchored to a consumer rather than a producer — the edge direction reverses.

recipes.text: Add a rate limiter in front of {0.label} (`{0.id}`) — public traffic is hitting it unthrottled.
recipes.why: A new SERVICE card that fronts an existing one; the added edge points INTO the real node.

recipes.text: The client is calling {0.label} (`{0.id}`) and {1.label} (`{1.id}`) directly. Put a backend-for-frontend in front of both.
recipes.why: One new node, two outbound edges — checks the model does not stop at one edge.

recipes.text: {0.label} (`{0.id}`) should own its data instead of sharing. Give it its own database.
recipes.why: Datastore card + a db_write-shaped edge label.

recipes.text: {1.label} (`{1.id}`) is hammering {0.label} (`{0.id}`) with reads. Add a read replica and point the read path at it.
recipes.why: The only recipe whose FIRST slot is a datastore — guards against a positional habit.

recipes.text: We need an audit trail of everything {0.label} (`{0.id}`) changes. Add somewhere to write it.
recipes.why: Vague, user-voice phrasing with no schema words in it at all — the realistic worst case.

recipes.text: Both {0.label} (`{0.id}`) and {1.label} (`{1.id}`) should report metrics somewhere central. Add the sink.
recipes.why: Fan-in to a single new node from two real ones.

recipes.text: We are retiring {0.label} (`{0.id}`). Show me the architecture with it gone.
recipes.why: The only recipe that should produce a non-empty removeCardIds. Without it the model learns the field is dead.

recipes.text: Replace {0.label} (`{0.id}`) with a managed equivalent — drop the one we run and add the one we call.
recipes.why: Removal AND addition in one proposal; the mixed case neither pure family covers.
